transcript:
Header:
Date: 2025-05-06
Time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 56m
Attendees: Alex Chen (Redwood AE), Maya Patel (Redwood SE), Jordan Lee (Acme - Head of ML), Priya Nair (Acme - Sec & Compliance), Sam Ortega (Acme - Platform)

Summary (auto): Quick scoping for a 2-week POC focused on data handling. Decision points: allow redaction, be explicit about retention, option to run in Redwood Private in VPC, run benchmarks with sample traffic.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Alex Chen: hey everyone thanks for joining, i think we have about 55, 56 minutes, quick intros, and then maya will go over the benchmark plan and i can cover the security stuff.
[00:12] Jordan Lee: thanks alex, jordan here, as a bit of context we want to evaluate redwood to handle question-answering over customer support transcripts; big concern is PII and retention because of reg constraints.
[00:22] Priya Nair: hi all, i'm priya our security lead, main ask is we need to ensure no persistent storage of raw prompts with customer-identifiable info, or at least redaction/hashing, and we need audit logs for every request.
[00:33] Maya Patel: great, so agenda - success criteria, workload size, benchmarks, timelines, and then data handling: redaction, logging, retention, prompt storage. i'll run through proposed benchmark matrix.
[00:47] Alex Chen: quick note - we typically offer hosted api, dedicated, and private. for POC we can run hosted with logging disabled, or Private in your VPC for strict controls. we'll propose both in the SOW.
[01:04] Sam Ortega: what would disable logging mean? do you still keep request traces for debugging? we have to provide e-discovery packets sometimes.
[01:13] Maya Patel: good question. we have modes: full logging, redacted logging, and no logging. redacted means we run a redaction pass on incoming prompts to strip tokens matching configured patterns (names, ssn patterns, email). redaction is deterministic so you can map back if needed via audit keys - but we can also provide hashed placeholders.
[01:36] Priya Nair: can you show how redaction works for complex fields like account numbers mixed with text? regex often misses things.
[01:46] Maya Patel: yes; we support both rule-based regex and ML-based PII detection. for tricky formats we recommend ML-based detection with a feedback loop. we can also export redaction logs to your S3 with KMS encryption.
[02:04] Jordan Lee: for success criteria, we want 95th percentile latency under 350ms for short prompts (<= 256 tokens) and end-to-end throughput to handle 20 reqs/sec sustained. accuracy is also key — F1 > 0.85 on our QA set.
[02:24] Alex Chen: that sounds reasonable. for 20 qps and 350ms p95, we'd probably recommend a dedicated pool for predictable performance; for the POC we can emulate with a small dedicated setup or run in hosted with guaranteed capacity.
[02:40] Maya Patel: benchmark plan proposal: 1) synthetic steady-state load at 20 rps with your prompt set, 2) spike tests to 100 rps for burst handling, 3) end-to-end latency including your auth and network hops, 4) embedding index write/read tests if you plan vector search. we'll instrument tokens/sec and cost per 1k tokens.
[03:05] Sam Ortega: how are prompts stored on your side if we keep logging on? do they go into long-term storage or ephemeral logs?
[03:15] Alex Chen: default hosted logging retains request/response logs for 30 days; they are encrypted at rest. for customers concerned about PII we'll either redact before storage or disable storage. for Private deployment, logs never leave your VPC unless you opt-in to send to Redwood.
[03:31] Priya Nair: need to confirm retention windows; our legal says certain logs must be kept for 1 year for e-discovery, but raw PII cannot be stored unredacted. can Redwood support configurable retention per log type?
[03:46] Maya Patel: yes, retention is configurable by route/model. you can set request logs to 0 days, 7 days, 30, 90, or custom with export to your S3. we have an audit trail feature that logs metadata (request id, user id hash, model/version) without storing raw prompt if you choose.
[04:05] Jordan Lee: about prompt storage - we also worry about prompt caching and whether cached prefixes could leak. does redwood persist cached prefixes across requests?
[04:16] Maya Patel: we have an optional KV cache for prefixes to speed up continuations. for POC we can disable shared KV caching or ensure per-customer isolation. cached keys are hashed and can be rotated; we can also configure TTL low so nothing is long-lived.
[04:33] Sam Ortega: embeddings: if we send vectors for vector DB building, do you keep vectors or do they return them and delete?
[04:42] Alex Chen: embeddings are treated as customer data. by default we do not use them to train models. for hosted we store embeddings per retention policy; for Private they stay in your infra. we can also offer a no-persist option where embeddings are returned and not stored.
[04:58] Priya Nair: KMS question - can we manage keys? and is there HSM support?
[05:05] Alex Chen: yes, Redwood supports customer-managed KMS for Private and Dedicated; HSM-backed keys can be integrated via our KMS connector. you'll find integration docs in the security pack we'll share.
[05:18] Jordan Lee: ok let's talk timelines - we want to run the POC in mid-may for 2 weeks and then present results to stakeholders. is that feasible?
[05:27] Alex Chen: yes, proposed timeline: this week finalize SOW and security checks, next week provision test env and run benchmarks (week of 2025-05-12), then 2-week POC starting 2025-05-19, results presentation week of 2025-06-02.
[05:45] Maya Patel: for the benchmark we need a sample corpus and expected answers to compute accuracy. jordan, can you share labeled QA pairs?
[05:53] Jordan Lee: yes i'll share a ~2k prompt set with labels, and we'll highlight fields that must be redacted.
[06:00] Priya Nair: we'll also draft a short list of compliance requirements and e-discovery scope.
[06:06] Alex Chen: note on training - Redwood does not use customer prompts to train models unless you opt into data sharing. for the POC we will set data-use to no-train.
[06:18] Jordan Lee: good. any constraints on prompt length? some of our transcripts are long, like 2k tokens.
[06:25] Maya Patel: our runtime supports long-context models; but cost and latency scale. for long transcripts we'll recommend pre-chunking and embedding-based retrieval augmented generation (RAG) to keep latency in check. we'll include that in the benchmark matrix.
[06:41] Sam Ortega: for the benchmarks, what metrics will you report back?
[06:46] Maya Patel: we'll report p50/p95/p99 latencies, tokens/sec, cost per 1k tokens, accuracy metrics you provide (F1/EM), memory usage, and any OOM or degradation events. we'll also capture logs for debugging but only as per your retention config.
[07:05] Priya Nair: is there a secure way to redact client identifiers prior to sending? we prefer client-side hashing before sending to minimize sharing raw PII.
[07:16] Alex Chen: yes, client-side hashing is supported; you can hash identifiers before sending. we also offer a server-side configurable redaction so you get both options. note: hashed values can break some QA tasks so we'll need to validate accuracy in the benchmark.
[07:34] Jordan Lee: about access controls - can we restrict who at Redwood can see logs or run queries against them?
[07:42] Maya Patel: yes, RBAC is enforced. for Private you control IAM; for Hosted we enforce least-privilege and can set roles for support access with just-in-time escalation and customer approval for any debug access.
[07:58] Alex Chen: competitor note - some folks consider internal self-host, openai + enterprise plugins; main differences are control over data and predictable cost. we'll put a short comparison in the SOW appendix.
[08:12] Sam Ortega: let's clarify acceptance criteria for the POC: 1) p95 under 350ms for short queries, 2) sustained 20 rps with no more than 5% error rate, 3) cost per 1k tokens < budget threshold (tbd), 4) redaction validated (no raw PII in stored logs) - ok?
[08:31] Alex Chen: yep that's perfect. add accuracy > 0.85 and agreement to no-train data use.
[08:38] Jordan Lee: agreed.
[08:40] Maya Patel: i'll outline the benchmark matrix and the exact scripts. we prefer to run tests from your VPC to include real network latency; sam will coordinate.
[08:50] Sam Ortega: yes i'll set up a bastion and ephemeral runners, we prefer the benchmark tool to be your standard k6 wrapper.
[08:59] Alex Chen: final note on prompts: some customers want Redwood to never persist raw prompts; we can sign that in an addendum. for the POC we'll include redaction + retention set to 7 days by default.
[09:11] Priya Nair: please share the redaction rules and any false-positive/negative rates for the ML detector.
[09:19] Maya Patel: will do; ML detector performance varies by domain, we'll include tuning guidance and a feedback loop to iteratively improve recall.
[09:29] Jordan Lee: last question - do you provide a way to prove deletion if needed?
[09:34] Alex Chen: yes, we provide deletion certificates and audit logs showing deletion operations along with KMS key rotation logs if you request them.
[09:42] Priya Nair: ok thanks, that helps.
[09:44] Alex Chen: great, to recap: alex sends security pack + SOW; maya sends benchmark runbook; jordan provides prompt set; sam provisions network; priya confirms retention policy. we aim to start benchmarks week of 5/12. any final comments?
[09:58] Jordan Lee: none, thanks everyone.
[10:01] Priya Nair: thanks.
[10:03] Alex Chen: thanks all, we'll follow up with links and next steps.

End of call.
